quest.title: A Faint Signal Lingers
quest.description: Xilonen has caught a glimpse of the Blazegem Inscriptions' forging process and has guessed what Tlazolli means to use them for. For safety reasons, she will dismantle this particular Inscription and analyze its inner workings first, and then decide whether to help Tlazolli save the gravely ill Nechca.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: A Prayer for Blessings, Told to Crested Peaks: Act III
chapter.title: Melodious Chant

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You two can wait outside for a moment — I just need to go in and grab something. The workshop is a little messy, so unfortunately, I won't be able to show you around.

choices.text: But I want to have a look!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Uh, that's not really what I mean... It's not the mess that's really the problem.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's just that the workshop is cluttered with way too much stuff... Books, files, and even ancient texts I got from Masters of the Night-Wind.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Everything's piled up to the ceiling. You probably won't know where to step once you're inside.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Kachina suffered quite an unfortunate series of events the last time she went inside... Ahem, I suppose it was my fault for being so focused on searching for information at the time that I forgot to lock the door...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: After entering the workshop, she was shocked to find herself face-to-face with a massive woven scroll from the Masters of the Night-Wind. Then, she turned around, and knocked over a huge stack of forging blueprints.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: She tried to step out of the way, but tripped on an poster tube that was behind her. And then, BOOM, the forging blueprints came crashing right onto her head.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no...

choices.text: That must've hurt!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: She's lucky I noticed in time. I found Kachina in a daze and managed to save her before an entire set of the History of the Children of Echoes was about to bury her... I then dragged her up to the second floor.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Ever since then, Kachina always waits outside the door, and doesn't dare take a step in whenever she comes to see me.

choices.text: Are there really that many books inside?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're an artisan and craftswoman, after all. We thought there would be weapons and armor hanging all over the place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it seems more like a library than a workshop.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Well, my primary work is forging Ancient Names, which is much trickier than making swords and tools. Aside from the necessary craftsmanship, I also need to consult many ancient texts.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You probably already know that each Ancient Name represents a certain "spirit," behind which are countless related stories to support it.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: In other words, the essence of an Ancient Name is the physical manifestation of a certain spiritual will.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And as a Name Engraver, when I'm working on a new Ancient Name, I'm not only trying to give it a physical shape...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But more importantly, I'm also trying to understand the spirit contained within the name.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And to do that, I have to collect as many related stories as possible, and read through them all.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But, as you might know, people tend to add a lot of... extraneous details when it comes to stories about themselves.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: For stories that have been clearly exaggerated or altered, I must gather other related stories or information as cross-references...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: This way, I can filter out all the absurd and exaggerated details, and restore the person's life to its true nature.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Only in true stories can you find the authentic spirit.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And this is the only way for the spirit to become an Ancient Name that matches its essence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've heard about the concept behind Ancient Names before, but after hearing you explain the details, Paimon can't help but think that Ancient Names are really powerful!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If only they could be even more powerful...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: No matter how powerful Ancient Names could be, they would never be able to suddenly turn into a blade, or allow you to smash through an entire cliff in one punch.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's just a form of spiritual power that's passed down from generation to generation. It doesn't have those kinds of physically tangible effects.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Um... Take your own names, for example.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: From the moment you appeared in this world, some person had already prepared a blessing for you.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That person then condensed this "blessing" into your name, and gave it to you as a gift.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It may feel like the moment you received your name is already in the past, but it will always stay with you, and move with you into the future.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: "Names are blessings for the future from people standing in the past." That's what Auntie once told me.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: With this blessing, people will become more confident as they walk into their future... To put it another way, it's like having a lamp in your hand as you walk through the darkness of night.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon gets that! If you're alone when you're walking in the dark, it's easy to get scared and tired quickly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if someone else is walking with you, then it won't be nearly as scary. And... well, you might still get tired, but it'll still be a whole lot better than walking alone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME} always has Paimon by {M#his}{F#her} side though, so {M#he}{F#she}'ll never have to worry about that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh, Paimon's sure many wish they could be in your shoes, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Please, you're always the one to get tired when we're on the road.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon's always flying! Of course it gets tiring... But we're getting off-topic! We can talk about that later...

choices.text: Try not to fall asleep on me next time...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Anyway, this is what Tlazolli told me when I was training as a Name Engraver.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: To be honest, I've only understood twenty percent of what she said at most. I've never been able to figure out the rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But doesn't that basically mean you don't get it!?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Well, that's not entirely true. Auntie and I have at least come to a consensus on the most important thing.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Ah, I'm sick of talking, we can talk about this more later. Please wait a moment while I grab my things.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Xilonen opens the door and walks into her workshop. Some unsettling crashing sounds come from the workshop, followed by some agonizing creaks and squeaks.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Eventually, Xilonen rushes out the door with a box in her arms. She then turns around and kicks the door closed, shutting the sound of dusty books falling to the ground inside...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you hear a whole section of something collapse in there just now?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: *coughs* It's fine, it's fine. It was just a bunch of very old Ancient Name records, I've already made copies of them.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I kept this set of Phlogiston Wedges in the back, so it wasn't easy to take out. I had to resort to brute force.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Come on, let's go disassemble the Central Inscription. It shouldn't take long.

choices.text: At least try not to eat so much...
I thought a workshop was supposed to be full of tools...
W—Was Kachina okay?
A mess is what I like best!

talks.objective: Help Xilonen dismantle the Blazegem Inscription

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Here we are, this is the place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This cliff is pretty high... What are we going to do here? Are we gonna climb to the very top and then throw this Inscription down the cliff?

choices.text: We're disassembling it, not destroying it, Paimon.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I'm going to use phlogiston to make an engraving circle on the cliff wall. That will allow me to investigate the internals of the Central Inscription.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Now let me see if this thing can even turn on. I was still an apprentice the last time I used it.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Before we attempt to engrave the inside pattern of an Ancient Name with phlogiston, we always use this to draw out the engraving diagram on a cliff or open ground.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Only after we've confirmed that phlogiston can flow properly through the internal engravings can we start formally working on the small internal engravings of the Ancient Name.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If we want to dismantle the Central Inscription in a non destructive manner, we'll have to use this thing... I really don't want to engrave such a large diagram with my bare hands.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you'll be able to see what it looks like on the inside without ruining Tlazolli's Inscription?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: For the most part. If it were just an ordinary unfinished Ancient Name piece, I'd just take it apart and pour phlogiston into the internal engravings to see everything.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But since it's the Central Inscription... It would be better not to destroy the blessing that Auntie has prepared for Nechca.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, Xilonen... Does this Central Inscription fall under the twenty percent you understand about Ancient Names, or the other eighty percent you don't understand?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's an eighty percent chance that it's part of the twenty percent.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Don't worry. As I said, Auntie and I share an understanding of the most important principle.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Which is... "Names are intrinsically valuable."

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Only by having names can things be sorted and categorized. They allow the world to become more orderly and identifiable.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: For example, when I order ore, I would usually say, "I need Volcanic Crystals of about thirty-five percent purity and no more than three percent of impurities."

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Without specific names, I would only be able to go to the ore merchant and say, "I want this, and this... No, this isn't it. That one? No, not that one either." You see what I mean?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Names are a crucial part of how we standardize our workflow. Without names, the work would be impossible.

choices.text: Hm, makes sense...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Yes, because forging Ancient Names is first and foremost a technical job. There's no debating that.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: As for the question of why it's important... As long as it does not affect your ability to perform the work, you'll gradually understand it as you put the process into practice.

choices.text: You really care about efficiency above all else...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: After all, creating an Ancient Name is quite the complicated process...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: *sigh* Let me break it down even further, we're not in the tribe right now anyway... Essentially, by forging Ancient Names, I'm assigning "nicknames" to the heroes in Natlan's history.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Giving someone a name is a subjective expression. You just need to express your hopes and wishes for them.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But giving someone a nickname is a much more objective expression. To come up with a fitting and accurate nickname requires much thought and observation.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If Ancient Names, or nicknames, aren't descriptive enough, no one will remember them anyway.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: So the best I can do is gather all the information I could, and try to come up with the most fitting nicknames possible.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Even a minor mistake in the process could cause people to misunderstand the nickname. For a Name Engraver such as myself, such mistakes would be considered a major blunder.

choices.text: Paimon! Nicknames are your specialty!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon isn't trying to come up with a nickname for Xilonen! Besides, all of Paimon's nicknames have been very descriptive. Everyone can remember them!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Now I'm curious. Why don't you come up with one for me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Are you serious!?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Of course. This is also my line of work, you know. Go ahead.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... A nickname... Xilonen... She uses phlogiston to forge weapons and make names for others...

choices.text: Don't over stress, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, uhhh... Smith?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hahaha. Not bad, not bad, and quite fitting, too. I'll remember it.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But you should keep observing my work, Paimon. Maybe you'll come up with an even better nickname.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Right, time to make like a "Smith" and start smithing. Watch closely.

choices.text: You'd better make it a good one.
See? Your nicknames need more thought and observation, Paimon!
Sounds like the most efficient approach...
So you're talking about it from a technical perspective...
I'm sure Xilonen knows what she's doing.

talks.objective: Hear Xilonen's conclusions after having disassembled and analyzed the Blazegem Inscription

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Amazing, Xilonen! You were running all over that cliff as if it was flat ground!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that the power of the Children of Echoes?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It doesn't have anything to do with my tribe. It's just the phlogiston adhesive I have on my shoes.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But after all that running around, I'll have to infuse them with more phlogiston again... I should prepare a spare supply of Phlogiston to bring with me next time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't tell me you're actually already covered head to toe in work equipment?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: More or less, yeah. I usually have at least the key equipment on hand.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I can show them to you when we next find the time. But let's get to work first.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Let me see... Start with anchor one, and activate it with density three phlogiston...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, a super huge diagram just appeared!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tlazolli's Central Inscription is even floating...!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Under Xilonen's guidance, the phlogiston engraving diagram on the cliffside remains stable as the Central Inscription is hit by massive amounts of Phlogiston at different frequencies.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After some time, the blasts of Phlogiston cease and the Central Inscription returns to Xilonen's hands.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So are you done checking the Inscription, Xilonen? How does it look?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I didn't find any anomalies in the Phlogiston Engraving. All the adjustments are indeed based on Ancient Name engraving techniques.

choices.text: So you're saying that everything's normal?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That means we can help Tlazolli and Nechca now, right?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Probably, but I have good news and bad news. Oh, but I'm also just going to go ahead and share both, so it's not like you'll have a choice in the matter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon will cover her ears after the good news...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #Even if you cover your ears, the issue will still continue to exist... But before we get to that, I want to ask {NICKNAME} a question.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: What are your thoughts on absorbing memories?

choices.text: It's necessary to save Nechca.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Sounds like something you would say.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But if you ask me, there's a problem with what Auntie said.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's hard to control the absorption of memories. Technically speaking, this type of Inscription has the power to do far more than absorb memories related to a single person.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: By herself, Auntie can't handle that level and scope of work, but if she has accomplices... It is completely possible for her to use this Inscription to accomplish far bigger things.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Accomplices... You make it sound like she's committing a crime...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Well, here's the good news. Yes, this Blazegem Inscription would be the perfect tool to commit crimes, but we haven't found any accomplices or signs that she intends to put it to such uses.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: From a purely objective standpoint, we can consider that possibility as "yet to be confirmed" for now.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The bad news is... there is still an underlying problem with this Blazegem Inscription that cannot be ignored.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I believe I've mentioned this before. Ancient Names operate with the help of the Wayob, granting them the power to read information kept in the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: In this process, the Wayob actually function like relays, helping the Ancient Name bearer sense the information from within the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If you remove the Wayob from the process and don't use any tools, then finding a specific story is akin to...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Trying to scoop up a specific grain of sand from a rushing river.

choices.text: So before you're even able to retrieve the sand...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Exactly. Anyone who attempts to do so will likely lose most of their cognitive function, or become a babbling madman who talks to themselves all day long.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Now, let's consider the memories that Auntie has gathered as the Ley Line, and Nechca as the only Ancient Name bearer of this Ley Line.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: There's no way Auntie would let Nechca plunge into the river of memories without any tools — she'd only be overwhelmed by the surge of memories.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And considering that Nechca has forgotten all of her past, she'll be unable to work on her own to accurately find the "correct past."

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Only Aunt Tlazolli can help her filter the correct memories of her past.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: So, if my hypothesis is correct, Auntie is actually planning on turning herself into Nechca's "Wayob" to help her extract the corresponding memories in the different situations she may face.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: In an ideal world, this would be perfectly fine. As long as every extracted memory is correct, Nechca would essentially be getting her past back.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: And I also believe that there won't be any mistakes in everything that Auntie remembers about Nechca.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But... Auntie is not a Wayob. Her body won't be able to handle the load for long.

choices.text: So at any moment, she might just...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But how can we solve this problem!? No matter how we try, Tlazolli will...

choices.text: She's already made up her mind.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: "Names are blessings for the future from people standing in the past"...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I've also made up my mind. C'mon, let's go see Auntie.

choices.text: She's ready to pay the price.
I see... This is the problem that we can't ignore.
You would most likely drown.
It somehow doesn't seem right.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I knew you felt the same way. That'll save me some initial explanation, I've never been very good at that anyway.

choices.text: So that means...

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Ah, Xilonen. It looks like... you've made your decision. Am I right?

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yes. Here's some research that I've done. You can reference it to modify the way the Central Inscription operates.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I'll also help you continue working on the Blazegem Inscription, but I must have complete control over all the Inscriptions, and the ability to oversee their uses.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: The memories that can be absorbed by the Inscription will be limited solely to Nechca's past. We'll plan a set timeframe together from which the memories can be drawn from shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: If you attempt to extract any memories beyond this scope, then I'll consider that as committing a criminal act, and halt all work related to the Central Inscription.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: After the memory bank is constructed, the Blazegem Inscriptions' absorption functions must be stopped immediately. Only functionalities for outputting memories will be kept.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I accept.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Thank you, Xilonen. I really...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Auntie, you know I can't stand it when you do this. If you needed my help, you should have just said so. There's no need to beat around the bush like you did.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Using technology for Ancient Names to forge other things without permission is no trivial matter. I...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Yes, it's a major departure from the technology's intended use. But it's nothing compared to a child who needs help... compared to a name that's about to be lost.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: But once this is all over, you must come with me to see Pacal and discuss everything that happened.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: That's fine. I'm willing to accept any punishment for my little Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Alright, let's clear off the table and come up with a plan...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I need some time to consider how to let Nechca control the Blazegem Inscription on her own and extract the memories from her past.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: By the way, did you give the book to Nechca?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: How could I just hand her a birthday present that you specially brought for her?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I've picked out a box and packaged it up. Wait till her birthday and then bring it to her, it'll be a nice surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: It's just an old book, there's no need to—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, is Nechca up again? But what was all that noise? It sounded like something broke.

choices.text: Oh no, did she fall?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh, that's not good! Let's go have a look!

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Nechca, don't hurt yourself!
Xilonen, is that you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, you're Nechca?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: How many times have I told you? Don't get out of bed on your own. You were running a fever yesterday.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Hello, Nechca.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: Thank you for the book, I've already read it several times.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You've already read it? But didn't Tlazolli package up the book that Xilonen brought?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: No, she's all mixed up. The one she read isn't from Xilonen, it's one I bought for her before.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: A few days ago, she told me she wanted a book. I know nothing about those kinds of books, so I had no choice but to go to the tribe and look for a copy.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I eventually found one and bought it for her. I put it in her room once I got back.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Soon after, she suddenly developed a fever. I was so busy taking care of her that I forgot about the book and even forgot that she had asked you for a gift.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Auntie, do you know which version of the book you bought?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Which version? The shopkeeper said it was the one with the "perfect" ending to the story. Apparently, that's the only one you can find on the market now.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Ugh, it's all my fault. You wasted your money, and now, it won't even be a surprise...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's alright, it's just a book. As long as Nechca enjoys it, that's what matters.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, Nechca probably doesn't know us. We're—

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: #You're Paimon and {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}! Mom told me about you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, hehe, seems like everyone knows who we are now.

choices.text: No need to introduce ourselves anymore.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Nechca seems to be doing pretty well today. Since she's been stuck indoors for the last few days, why don't we take her out for a walk?

choices.text: Let's check your temperature...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Take her for a walk... But, considering her condition, I don't think she—

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: #Don't worry, Auntie. She'll be safe with {NICKNAME} and me.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: We won't leave the tribe, and if anything comes up, we'll be sure to find the doctor immediately.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Besides, it's her birthday in a few days, and we need to go to the tribe to buy some things. Let's give her a proper celebration.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: What do you think, Auntie?

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: I promise I'll be good, Mom.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: Didn't you say before that I need more fresh air?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Alright, alright. As you wish.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I also happen to have a few repaired Blazegem Inscriptions that I need to get back to the tribe. We can go together.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Wait for a moment. I'll go get Nechca's water bottle and some towels... Ah, some medicine... Oh, and a parasol.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tlazolli enters Nechca's room. After quickly packing, she comes back out...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Talk about being prepared...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We can camp out with all that stuff.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: It doesn't hurt to be prepared. Okay, let's go. Please be good, now, Nechca. Don't cause any trouble for Xilonen and the others.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You can let me carry these. Don't be a stranger, Nechca, feel free to tell us anything. Even I was quite a handful for Auntie when I was little.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, yeah! It's not often you get to go out to play, so just have fun! Everything will be fine.

choices.text: If you don't stir up some trouble when you're little...

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: Okay. Thanks, everyone. And please don't worry, Mom.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: I'll be good.

choices.text: Then you'll never get the chance again.
Seems the fever's gone.
Hello, Nechca.
Maybe she knocked something over?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh! What if something fell on her? We should check. Paimon will go have a look!

talks.objective: Give the Blazegem Inscription back to Iknal

dialogues.speaker: Iknal
dialogues.text: Tlazolli, what brings you to the tribe today? Oh? And Nechca, too!

dialogues.speaker: Iknal
dialogues.text: She seems to be doing much better now! She's even out and about. I'm sure it won't be long before she'll be playing with Chanil and the others.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I hope so. Here, Iknal, this is your Inscription. I've finished repairing it.

dialogues.speaker: Iknal
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you for bringing it back for me. By the way, I came across a piece of good-quality ore a while ago. I was thinking of using it to make some pretty jewelry for little Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Iknal
dialogues.text: I remember that Nechca would become so happy every time she saw a shiny ring. Right, Nechca?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I'm sure she'd love that, thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Iknal
dialogues.text: My pleasure. Give me a moment, I'll bring the ore.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I can make the jewelry for her. What kind would you like, Nechca?

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: I would like...

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Something shaped like an Embercore Flower would be nice. She was always asking me before to make her an Ancient Name with an Embercore Flower design.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Noted. I'll make that as a gift for her next birthday.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Sorry, Nechca. It won't be a surprise for you.

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: ...That's okay. Thank you, Xilonen.

dialogues.speaker: Iknal
dialogues.text: Found it! Sorry to keep you waiting. Here, please take it.

dialogues.speaker: Iknal
dialogues.text: By the way, Nechca, feel free to write to me if you ever want to know more about ores.

dialogues.speaker: Iknal
dialogues.text: I was shocked last time when you wrote me out of the blue asking for a Volcanic Crystal.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: *sigh* Sorry about that. She can hardly contain her curiosity now that she's started to recover.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: She's still too weak to go out whenever she wants, so she begs me every day to help her write letters to people in the tribe about all sorts of things.

dialogues.speaker: Iknal
dialogues.text: Hahaha! That's how you know she's one of the Children of Echoes. It's normal for us to be interested in ore.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everything's looking up. Hehe, we're just like the main character in the new version of Tequil the Brave when he was about to save his brother, Rimac.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to the story, we should be right around... Hmm, let Paimon see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Tequil prayed to the Goddess of Mountains and Fire, 'Let my brother's name ever live on. I am willing to sacrifice my heart and blood in return.'"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The Goddess replied, 'I've heard your prayer, but your brother is no longer your kin. His name has sunken into the deepest of depths.'"

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: Then, Tequil said...

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: "Turn my blood to fire, so my heart may illuminate the depths. I will bring my brother back before my blood runs dry."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! You remembered that whole line, Nechca! Paimon remembers that's exactly what the book... Huh? Wait, what did the book say?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You forgot? But didn't you just read it, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon finished both books in one sitting! A lot of their content is nearly the same, so it's easy to get mixed up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But the ending in the older version is more interesting. Even if it's hard for kids to, well... completely understand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, wait! Nechca hasn't read the other ending... It's okay! Just wait a bit, and Paimon will read it out for you!

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: Th—That's not true. Actually... I already know the other ending.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You already know the other ending? But didn't you only read the edition your Mom got for you...?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you all chatting about so happily?

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: #Mom... {M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME} and I were just talking about the ending of that book.

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: We were just talking about how the bad guy was defeated and everyone returned home safely... It's a really happy ending.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Aren't happy endings always nice? But if you already read the whole thing, then what will Mom have to read to you at bedtime?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Guess you'll have to go to bed early tonight. But I'll buy you some more fairy tales next time, okay?

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: Okay, Mom...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, how's the ore?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It's pretty good quality. I'll be able to give Nechca a beautiful and durable piece of jewelry for her next birthday.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: But for now, let's focus on celebrating her upcoming birthday. Where are we headed next, Auntie?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Next, let's visit Apoxpalon, he should be close by.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Stay close, Nechca. Don't go too far.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: Yes, Mom...

choices.text: (That's... not the "other ending" she was talking about.)

talks.objective: Give the Blazegem Inscription back to Apoxpalon

dialogues.speaker: Apoxpalon
dialogues.text: Why do my eyebrows keep twitching today? Strange...

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: That means you're about to hit the jackpot, Apoxpalon.

dialogues.speaker: Apoxpalon
dialogues.text: Haha, I didn't expect to have two Name Engravers coming in today. Welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Apoxpalon
dialogues.text: What are you looking to buy, Tlazolli? I'll give you a discount like usual!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, offering a discount just like that? Tlazolli sure has connections...

dialogues.speaker: Apoxpalon
dialogues.text: She was once our Name Engraver, and did a lot for the tribe. It's only fair that I offer her a discount.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Thank you for your generosity... I've finished repairing your Blazegem Inscription. Here, have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Come on Nechca, say thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: Thank you, sir...

dialogues.speaker: Apoxpalon
dialogues.text: Oh, so this is Nechca? Tlazolli has shown me some pictures before.

dialogues.speaker: Apoxpalon
dialogues.text: It looks like you are doing much better now. How about this? Go ahead and pick anything you'd like from the store. Think of it as a gift from me.

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: No, no, that's alright. Mom told me that you've already given a lot to our family.

dialogues.speaker: Apoxpalon
dialogues.text: Well, that was for your family. I've never given anything just for you. If you don't feel like it, you can also let your Mom choose for you.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: No need to stand on ceremony, Auntie. Go ahead and pick something for Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: His drills and small clamps are good quality. The measurements of each part are exact, and they are always very durable.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I always come here to buy things if I find myself in a pinch.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Do you have any child-friendly safety scissors? I remember seeing a few different styles.

dialogues.speaker: Apoxpalon
dialogues.text: I have a few in stock, but I put them in the back. Let me bring some out for you to pick.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: No need to bring them all the way here. Why don't we just go in the back and choose there? It should only take a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I don't know much about that kind of scissors, why don't you just go yourself and...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: There are too many different designs and varieties of kid's scissors. If you don't come and help me choose, I won't be able to pick one that Nechca would like.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Come on, Auntie. It'll only take a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There goes Xilonen dragging Tlazolli off to buy more stuff. What a busy day...

choices.text: Let's just wait for them here.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: I won't run off. Um, Paimon... who's your favorite character in Tequil the Brave?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's favorite? Tequil of course! He went through a lot to rescue his family.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In the old version of the story, he was never able to reunite with his family... But he was still really strong and fought as best as he could.

choices.text: He's a brave character.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about you, Nechca? Which character do you like?

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: I... I like Rimac.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... the one who was possessed by Coatlicue but never forgot his brother Tequil. He was also an amazing character!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If it wasn't for his determination, both he and his brother would have been defeated by Coatlicue in the final battle.

choices.text: Wow, you remember all the details, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! A story's only interesting if you can really get immersed in it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey Nechca, why don't we play pretend? You can be Rimac, and Paimon will be Tequil, okay?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You just like reciting epic lines.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}... Can I play the role of Coatlicue?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But isn't she the villain? In the old version, she even ate Rimac and took on his appearance.

choices.text: You said it yourself. That's the old version.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, right. She read the version with a happy ending... In that one, Coatlicue was defeated and the brothers both survived.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it doesn't matter, only the lines at the end were different. You can go ahead and say your favorite lines, Nechca. Paimon's read both versions, so she'll be able to play along.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: My favorite line is the one from the end! It's...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Come here, Nechca. Look at you... You're sweating.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: Mom!

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Let me wipe your forehead. Now, drink some water. This child... You forget everything as soon as you start playing.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: We've picked something out for Nechca. Apoxpalon will deliver it to Auntie's house once he's packaged it up. How was Nechca?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We were just about to get to the exciting part...

choices.text: Xilonen, did you leave us with Nechca on purpose?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, really? Oh, now that Paimon thinks about it, Xilonen has dragged Tlazolli away from us a couple of times now. But why?

choices.text: Nechca has a strange look on her face...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Let's talk later. Just trust me, and act normal for now.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: We should head to our last stop, Auntie. It's real hot today, and we shouldn't let Nechca be in the heat for too long.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Right, let's go see Cheven and head back home.

choices.text: Seems like she has something to say.
So we could talk with her alone?
That wasn't the one Nechca read.
Seems like you were really immersed in the story.
I admire his courage.
Be sure to stay close, Nechca.

talks.objective: Give the Blazegem Inscription back to Cheven

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: I've finished repairing your Blazegem Inscription, Cheven. I've also reinforced it, so it shouldn't fall apart so easily now.

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: Thank you... How about the Volcanic Crystal? Was it usable?

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Yes, thanks for that.

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: You're welcome. I just want to see Nechca get better.

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: Thank you, Miss Cheven...

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's fine. Honestly, you're both too polite for your own good...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: I was wondering where you got the ore for such a large-scale Blazegem Inscription.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: So you must be one of Tlazolli's accomplices, then?

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: Oh, Xilonen... um...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: We already know what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're all doing our best for Nechca.

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: Whew, you had me worried there! I thought we'd been found out... We'd be in real trouble if Pacal ever got wind of it.

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: To be honest, I won't be able to cover it up for much longer. I've been traveling away from home every few days, and the ore reserves have noticeably decreased...

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: The last time Pacal came and asked me about it, I could only say that I'd been using up a lot of ore to research new styles of jewelry...

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: As for why I had been leaving so often, I said that I had found a new ore vein and wanted to extract some new gems from it.

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: Ah, sorry... I've been talking my head off. Please come in and have a seat.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Sure, we can sit for a moment, but...

dialogues.speaker: Nechca
dialogues.text: Miss Cheven, can I... go see some of the jewelry over there?

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: You mean Imix's work? Sure, go ahead. Remember to stay in the shade as much as you can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wants to go, too! We'll go together. Paimon hasn't looked at Natlan's jewelry very closely yet.

choices.text: I'll have to buy you some.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Then Paimon's gonna take a good look at what they have.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You haven't bought any jewelry for a while, Auntie. Why don't you pick one out?

choices.text: (Xilonen's taking Tlazolli with her again...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, Nechca. We don't know anything about Natlan's jewelry, so you can help us pick something out!

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: #{M#Mr.}{F#Miss} {NICKNAME}, I...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Come here, Nechca.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Sorry, Cheven and Xilonen, but it's already getting late. We should be heading back now.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: It'll be Nechca's birthday in a few days, and there's still a lot for us to do before then...

response.speaker: Cheven
response.text: No problem, I'll be sure to bring her some beautiful jewelry to celebrate.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: Mom, I...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: You're getting hot again... Here, Mom will carry you. Let's get going.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: You forget to take care of yourself once you start playing. Let's go back and we'll have a talk.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: I... I didn't...

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Nechca, I never taught you to lie.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: S—Sorry, Mom. I... I...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nechca's looking at us... Paimon feels like something's not right. What should we do?

choices.text: ...Just wait.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Nechca was having so much fun today that she forgot the time. It's not a big deal.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Let me help carry her home. I'm worried you would also have to recover if you carried her the whole way.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: No, it's fine. I'll carry her.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Let's go, Nechca. It's time to go home.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tlazolli declines your help and leaves the tribe, carrying Nechca. She is staggering somewhat by the time she reaches home, but she is still able to shield Nechca behind her...

choices.text: Stay quiet. Let's see what Xilonen says.
(Let's keep talking with Nechca...)
If the price is good, we could buy you a whole set.

talks.objective: Go back to Tlazolli's house together

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Thank you, everyone, for spending so much time with us today.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Please be sure to come to Nechca's birthday party.

choices.text: We'll be there.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Alright, it's nearly bedtime for Nechca, so let's part our ways here.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Auntie, remember to give her the book that copy of Tequil the Brave I brought. I went to a lot of trouble to find it.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I understand. Really, do you think I'd let your efforts go to waste?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: It's very special to receive a book from you, I'm sure she'll put it somewhere safe... Right, Nechca?

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: Y—Yeah. Thanks, Xilonen...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Put it somewhere? Isn't she going to read it?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Well, I've read the story to her many times already, she's even memorized nearly every line...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That won't be a problem, Auntie. Nechca has probably never heard this version of Tequil the Brave.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Oh? What's different about this version?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The majority is about the same, but the ending is different from the one that you bought her.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The one I gave her is the unedited version that was originally published.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It was released long before Nechca fell ill.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Oh? But I remember you were never very interested in fairy tales, Xilonen.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Well, I was just thinking that if what you said about Nechca's illness is true, she shouldn't be able to remember anything about her past before her illness...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: So, the ending to the original version of Tequil the Brave is also part of the past that she should have forgotten.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: In other words, if she hasn't recently read the old version of the story, then she couldn't possibly know the ending, right?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: I don't understand. Why are you so concerned about the ending of this book? Even if she does remember the ending, what does that prove?

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Maybe she snuck out somewhere when I wasn't watching, and read the first edition of the story.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: That is a possibility. After all, she does remember things that have happened recently.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: In which case, let's go ask around the tribe and see if anyone remembers Nechca reading that book.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: There are only a few shops in the tribe that sell books. Or, we can just ask Nechca where she had read it.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: The book sellers all have Inscriptions, so there's a chance that their memories...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: So, you admit that the Blazegem Inscriptions can also affect the tribe's current memories?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: I was very clear that I would consider that a crime, and would put a stop to all work on it.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: ...There must be a few more books at home, I...

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: "I do not wish to see your blood be reduced to ash, but I have seen the light of your heart and spirit..."

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: ...I beg your pardon?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Nechca, where did you read that book? Answer me.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Go home, Nechca.

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Are you disobeying me?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: You're the one who wrote me the letter, Nechca. You're the one who wanted the book. Only you can speak for yourself.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: We're listening, Nechca. Right here, right now.

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: "...Remember my name, brother. As long as you remember me, I will never have left."

response.speaker: Tlazolli
response.text: Silence!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's the line from the old ending! Nechca remembers it!

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: I know! I know everything! Xilonen, help me! Please help me!

response.speaker: Nechca
response.text: Ahhh!!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Something's blocking the door!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Get back.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Without hesitation, Xilonen strides forward and kicks the door, shattering it and the surrounding structure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Xilonen! Wait for us!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: The tunnel is blocked. We can't go in... there might also be traps.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, what are all those things on Nechca's walls?

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: It seems Auntie put all the extra Inscriptions she made here.

choices.text: There's no one here!

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: If she's trying to finish that Ancient Name, then there's only one place she could go.

response.speaker: Xilonen
response.text: Come on, follow me.

choices.text: Where did they go?
I hope she'll continue to feel better.

dialogues.speaker: Cheven
dialogues.text: Nechca is finally better. Phew... I hope this is over soon, I can't keep this up much longer...

choices.text: About the sales plan for the Inscriptions...

response.speaker: Cheven
response.text: Hm? "Make 'em few, and sell 'em high"? Uh... I definitely never suggested anything like that to Tlazolli.

response.speaker: Cheven
response.text: Quite the opposite, I've always been telling her to make more inscriptions and expand her market. Maybe that way, she could even sell to other tribes.

response.speaker: Cheven
response.text: Wouldn't that be a lot more profitable? But she always says she has limited energy, and can't forge them...

response.speaker: Cheven
response.text: *sigh* Maybe taking care of Nechca is too tiring...

choices.text: See you later.

response.speaker: Cheven
response.text: Alright, I should be getting back to work now too. Now, why did I put the ore from before...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Let's head back to the tribe first. There are some things I need to get from my workshop.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Disassembling the Central Inscription... It's not gonna be easy.

dialogues.speaker: Tlazolli
dialogues.text: Let's go look for Iknal. I've had her Blazegem Inscription for a while now, and I'll finally return it to her today.
